newsitem.title: LEBANON: Malaysia PM promotes investment in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM promotes investment in Lebanon.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Monday began a three-day official visit to Lebanon intended to promote Malaysian investment in the Middle Eastern country.
Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, who visited Malaysia in 1995, greeted Mahathir at the airport.

Mahathir's delegation, which included four government ministers and representatives of the private sector, was to have talks with Lebanese economic and financial authorities to assess investment opportunities.
Mahathir, 71, is mixing holidays and official business during two months of foreign travel.

His visit will include a tour of the Beirut central district badly damaged in the 1975-90 civil war and being rebuilt by the Lebanese real estate company Solidere in what is billed as the world's largest urban redevelopment of the 1990s.
The project is the flagship of the multi-billion dollar reconstruction programme Hariri launched when he became prime minister in October 1992.
Hariri is said by the Lebanese media to be an admirer of Malaysia since his 1995 visit, which bolstered ties and brought agreements on investment guarantees, dual taxation and civil aviation.

Several Malaysia delegations have visited Lebanon since 1995 seeking investment opportunities linked to the reconstruction programme. Lebanese businessmen have also visited Malaysia to market products.
